items.followUp: Describe the light reactions of photosynthesis and summarize how carbon dioxide is converted into carbohydrates in the Calvin cycle.

rubric.why: These points define the locations and basic roles of both reaction stages.
rubric.description: Identifies the light and dark reactions.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that light reactions occur in the thylakoids and that dark reactions occur in the stroma and use ATP and NADPH.

rubric.why: This is the carbon-fixation step of the Calvin cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that carbon dioxide combines with RuBP and the resulting unstable compound splits to form PGA.

rubric.why: ATP and NADPH from the light reactions provide what is needed to reduce PGA.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ATP and NADPH are used to convert PGA into PGAL (G3P).

rubric.why: The cycle produces sugars and regenerates its carbon dioxide acceptor.
rubric.description: States sugar formation and RuBP regeneration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that some PGAL forms sugars and the remainder regenerates RuBP.

modelAnswer: Light reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes (grana) and require light; they produce ATP and NADPH and release oxygen from the splitting of water.
Dark reactions (the Calvin cycle) occur in the stroma. They do not require light directly and use ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide.
Carbon dioxide combines with RuBP, forming an unstable six-carbon compound that splits into two molecules of PGA.
ATP and NADPH reduce PGA to PGAL (G3P).
Some PGAL is used to form sugars, while the rest regenerates RuBP.

items.followUp: What is exocytosis? Name its two main types.

rubric.why: Endocytosis brings substances into the cell by enclosing them with the cell membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the cell membrane enclosing substances and bringing them into the cell in a vesicle.

rubric.why: These are the two types of endocytosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both phagocytosis and pinocytosis.

modelAnswer: Endocytosis is the process by which a cell takes substances in when its membrane surrounds them and forms a vesicle, bringing them into the cell.
Its types are phagocytosis and pinocytosis.

items.followUp: Define a co-enzyme and name two examples.

rubric.why: A co-enzyme is an organic molecule that assists an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a co-enzyme as an organic, non-protein molecule that assists an enzyme.

rubric.why: NAD, FAD and co-enzyme A are examples of co-enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming any two valid examples.

modelAnswer: A co-enzyme is a small organic, non-protein molecule that assists an enzyme in carrying out its function.
Examples include NAD, FAD and co-enzyme A.
